entry.title: Modelling the refractive index measurement of glass by using Dirichletian Process Mixture Model (DPMM)
entry.content:
Modellingthe refractive index measurement of glass by using Dirichletian ProcessMixture Model (DPMM)

Background

When glass is broken, some fragments of glass travel backwards andland on the surface of the breaker’s clothing or someone nearby. Thesetiny fragments may persist on the clothing for a period of time andfinding them can be used as evidence of proximity. In forensicexaminations, the physical properties of recovered glass fragments aremeasured and compared to glass collected from crime scenes. There aremany physical characteristics, such as color, thickness and surfacefeature that we can use for discrimination. However, the recovered glassis usually tiny, hence these characteristics cannot be access reliably.The refractive index can still be measured for a small pieces of glassfragment hence it is widely used as evidence in the interpretation ofglass.

When glass fragments are recovered from a suspect (recoveredsamples), and few broken window glass fragments is collected (controlsamples), the question often arise is that whether the recovered glassfragment is originated from the window glass. To do this, we can measurethe RI of them, and compare these measurement. A refractive measurementis a ratio (number) that describe how the light bends when it travelthrough the material:

\[\text{RI} = \frac{\text{Speed of lighttravel in vacuum}}{\text{Speed of light travel inmaterial}}\]

We can obtain the RI measurements of both the recovered samples andthe control samples, and then conduct the a test, such as T-test andWelch-T test. They can quantify the weight of evidence of howsimilar/dissimilar of these two groups of samples of glass.

However, another question also might be asked is: how rare of therecovered glass. The reason of asking such a question is that: if theglass is rare, then we want to assign a higher evidential value becauseit is unlikely to be found in the general population; Conversely, wewant the evidential value to be smaller if it is a common glass. Thisquestion needs to be address by conducting surveys of RI measurement ofdifferent sources of glass, and we can then model the distribution toobtain the point estimate for a glass fragment with a particular RImeasurement. The modelling procedure can be conducted by using ahistogram; However, a histogram may fit inconsistently as the choice ofbin-width is arbitrary. Secondly, histogram is a discreteapproach, hence there might be some region whether the estimatedprobability density is 0. -- This is because there are no observationfall in such a region. This 0 estimation may results the finialquantitation to be infinity therefore it is necessary to avoid thiscase. We solve this problem by using a Dirichletian Process MixtureModel (DPMM).

The core is this algorithm is to employ the Normalized CrossCorrelation (NCC) to compare the features of shoeprints extracted byusing a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). There are notraining process in this algorithm. The algorithm is as follows：

There are serval reasons/motivations that why The algorithm isdeveloped is in this way. First, there are limited shoeprint images arepublic available, the dataset we mainly used is called FID-300 that consists of ~ 1000reference shoeprint and ~ 300 crime scene shoeprint. A referenceshoeprint is a clean-full impression that are usually high-quality,while a crime scene shoeprint can be partial, distorted and taken underpoor condition. I personally (subjectively) think It is difficult totrain a general shoeprint image retrieval model with such a dataset withlimited images. Second,A pre-trained CNN model effectively capturescomplex patterns and textures in shoeprints, essential for identifyingunique characteristics like tread patterns and wear marks. Leveragingits training on diverse datasets, the model generalizes well to newdata, enabling efficient and accurate feature extraction for shoeprintimage retrieval.

A CNN feature consists of three dimensions (width \(\times\) height \(\times\) channel) -- withheight and width to be the dimension of the shoeprintimages (usually smaller than original images as there will be poolinglayers), and channel is the number of features. This can befound in the last layer in CNN that is used. For example, if we use theConv3_512 layer in the following VGG19 consists many CNNlayers, then the Channel will be 512, and similarChannel = 128 if we used the Conv3_128 as the lastlayer.

The image features of shoeprint images are then compared andsummarized into a single score. The main challenge here is the the imagefeature is a 3D array, while NCC can only work with 2D images.Furthermore, there are some features are mostly blank -- all pixelintensities equal to 0.
